sheet-1-1.description: The lower two thirds of sheet 1, drawn at 50 ft to an inch below a heavy line that separates it from the title block, key map and street index, cover the centre of Delanco south of Burlington Avenue (St. Mihiel Drive). Union Avenue runs down the middle of the part. To its east, square blocks between Union Avenue and Walnut Street are crossed by Chestnut and Hickory and split by the narrow Walnut Alley; block 13 holds the large brick Walnut Street School with its auditorium and class rooms, and block 16 the Delanco Public School and the frame Delanco Town Hall. A compass rose and the scale of feet are printed in block 16. West of Union Avenue the streets run on a diagonal grid: Buttonwood, Ash Alley, Ash and Vine cross the part from the south-west, with Poplar Street and Poplar Alley at the bottom. These blocks are mostly frame dwellings with outbuildings, a concrete-block store with auto repairing at Burlington Avenue, a milk depot, and the brick Fire Department of the Washington Fire Co. near Union Avenue. Block 19 appears in the upper left corner with a single large building, the Delanco A. A. Club House shown in full on the inset. Water pipes of 4 to 12 inches are drawn along the streets with town hydrants. The bottom left corner is taken by a framed inset (part 2) of the rest of block 19, and adjoining sheets 2, 3, 5, 6 and 7 are referenced around the edges.
notes: Printed sheet number 1; the upper part of the sheet carries the key map at 700 ft to an inch, the index and the title block and is not part of this annotation.
Walnut Alley is the modern Walnut Alley; Chestnut and Hickory are Chestnut Street and Hickory Street.
The modern junction of Chestnut Street and Walnut Alley lies about 7.6 m from where the sheet draws it and was not used.
Walnut Street School, Delanco Public School, Delanco Town Hall and the Washington Fire Co. fire house are on this part.

Map, 50 ft. Top third is the title block, a key map of the town (700 ft to an inch, not configured), water and fire notes, legend and street index; the map below a heavy line shows Burlington Av (St. Mihiel Drive), Buttonwood, Ash, Ash Alley, Vine, Union Av, Walnut Alley, Walnut, Chestnut, Hickory, Poplar St. Two parts: part 1 the main map, part 2 a framed inset at bottom left showing the west part of block 19 (Burlington Av bend at Willow St, Vine, Buttonwood, Poplar Alley), drawn at the same orientation but displaced on the page.

sheet-1-2.description: A small framed inset in the lower left corner of sheet 1, drawn at 50 ft to an inch and at nearly the same orientation as the main map but displaced on the page, completes block 19, of which the main map shows only the north-east corner. The block lies at the bend of Burlington Avenue (St. Mihiel Drive), where the avenue turns from its east-west course south-westward towards Vine, and Willow Street leaves the bend to the north-east. Vine runs along the south-west side of the block and Buttonwood along its south-east side. The block is mostly open ground, marked vacant beyond its eastern lot line. Along Burlington Avenue stand a brick store (numbers 25 and 66), a frame store with a dwelling (65) and another store and dwelling (64) with sheds. In the interior and towards Buttonwood stand the Delanco A. A. Club House, a large one-storey frame building, the small frame Public Library near Vine, and several dwellings with automobile garages. A north arrow is drawn inside the inset. Sheet numbers 2, 3 and 5 printed in the inset mark the adjoining sheets that draw the surrounding streets. The inset is bounded by a heavy frame line, and the part of the sheet outside it belongs to the main map (part 1).
notes: The inset was placed from four corners of the Delanco A. A. Club House carried from the main map of the sheet (part 1), which draws the same building; it has no detected street junction.
The club house is drawn about 4 percent smaller on the inset than on the main map, so the inset's fitted scale (7.49 px per ft) is below the sheet's (7.84).
Delanco A. A. Club House and the Public Library are on this inset.

Map, 50 ft. Top third is the title block, a key map of the town (700 ft to an inch, not configured), water and fire notes, legend and street index; the map below a heavy line shows Burlington Av (St. Mihiel Drive), Buttonwood, Ash, Ash Alley, Vine, Union Av, Walnut Alley, Walnut, Chestnut, Hickory, Poplar St. Two parts: part 1 the main map, part 2 a framed inset at bottom left showing the west part of block 19 (Burlington Av bend at Willow St, Vine, Buttonwood, Poplar Alley), drawn at the same orientation but displaced on the page.

sheet-2.description: Sheet 2, drawn at 50 ft to an inch, covers the north-west corner of Delanco along the Delaware River. Delaware Avenue runs along the river bank at the top, with a row of small frame dwellings on the river side. Below it, 2nd Street runs east to west across the right half and bends south-west at Cedar towards Orchard; 3rd Street does the same further south, its western leg running down to Vine. Willow runs down the right edge and turns south-west at the bottom towards Burlington Avenue, whose name appears in the lower right corner. Orchard enters at the left edge between 2nd Street and Vine. The blocks are large and thinly built: block 53 (formerly 54) on the river front is mostly open with a few scattered dwellings, block 21 is almost empty and carries the compass rose, and blocks 5 and 6 east of Cedar have a few large dwellings and a row of six attached dwellings facing Willow. Block 20 between 3rd Street, Vine and Willow is the most built up, with frame dwellings, automobile garages and one brick-veneered house. A note at the left edge reads vacant to Vine Street. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches and a few town hydrants are drawn along the streets. Sheet numbers 3 and 4 mark the adjoining sheets to the east and south. The sheet carries the Delanco N.J. August 1927 cartouche and the scale of feet.
notes: Cedar is the modern Cedar Street, Orchard is Orchard Avenue, Willow is Willow Street, Vine is Vine Street.
The left margin note reads 'Vacant to Vine St.'
Map, 50 ft. Northwest corner of the town along the Delaware River: Delaware Av, 2nd St, Cedar, 3rd St, Willow, Orchard, Vine, Burlington Av. Much open land west of Cedar. One part.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3, drawn at 50 ft to an inch, covers the central blocks of Delanco from the Delaware River to Burlington Avenue (St. Mihiel Drive), between Willow on the west and Walnut on the east. Delaware Avenue runs along the top with the river beyond, then 2nd Street and 3rd Street cross the sheet; Union Avenue runs down the middle, Linden splits the north-east blocks, and Willow bends south-west below 3rd Street. The blocks are residential: frame dwellings on regular lots with automobile garages behind, a few brick-veneered houses facing Delaware Avenue in block 4, and larger dwellings on the river front blocks 3 and 4. Block 11 on the south-east holds the Dobbins M.E. Church with its parsonage, and a plumber's shop stands on 2nd Street in block 8A. Block 12 on the south-west is lined with small attached and detached dwellings along Burlington Avenue. Water pipes of 4 to 12 inches and town hydrants are drawn along the streets, and an extension of 75 ft is noted at the head of Union Avenue on the river bank. Buttonwood Street, Ash Alley and Walnut Alley are named where they leave Burlington Avenue at the bottom edge. A compass rose stands at the left, the scale of feet at the bottom left, and sheet numbers 2 and 7 mark the adjoining sheets.
notes: Linden is the modern Linden Avenue; Willow and Walnut are Willow Street and Walnut Street.
Union Avenue is noted '75' extended' at the river bank.
Dobbins M.E. Church and its parsonage are on this sheet.
Map, 50 ft. Delaware Av to Burlington Av between Willow and Walnut: 2nd and 3rd Sts, Union Av, Linden. Dobbins M.E. Church. One part; pilot sheet.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4, drawn at 50 ft to an inch and turned on the page so that north points to the upper right, covers the western end of Delanco between Rancocas Creek and Vine. The Delaware River runs along the top right corner and Rancocas Creek down the whole left side. Orchard crosses the sheet near the top; below it Rancocas Avenue, Washington and Walter Avenue run down the sheet to Burlington Avenue (St. Mihiel Drive) at the bottom, with Vine along the right edge and a stub of 3rd Street leaving Vine. Franklin Street is named where it leaves Burlington Avenue at the bottom. Blocks 52A and 52B between Orchard and the river are large open grounds with a few dwellings, a windmill and the Inter-Nos Club House. Along the creek bank in block 24B stand a row of club houses and boat houses, one with a platform on the water. The blocks between Orchard and Burlington Avenue (24A, 23 and 22) are residential, with frame dwellings on narrow lots, garages, a few brick and one concrete-block dwelling, and rows of attached dwellings facing Burlington Avenue. A store stands at the corner of Rancocas Avenue and Burlington Avenue. The steel and wood drawbridge to Riverside is noted at the bottom left. Water pipes and hydrants are drawn along the streets, and the compass rose and scale of feet are printed in the corners.
notes: Orchard is the modern Orchard Avenue; Washington is Washington Street.
The modern junction of Burlington Avenue and Rancocas Avenue lies several metres west of the drawn one and was not used.
The Inter-Nos Club House and a row of club houses and boat houses on Rancocas Creek are on this sheet.
A note at the bottom left reads 'Steel & Wood Drawbridge to Riverside'.

Map, 50 ft, turned on the page (north toward the upper right; fitted rotation about 91 degrees). Orchard, Rancocas Av, Washington, Walter Av and Vine between the Delaware River and Burlington Av, with club houses along Rancocas Creek. One part.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5, drawn at 50 ft to an inch and turned like sheet 4, covers the blocks south of Burlington Avenue (St. Mihiel Drive) between Rancocas Creek and Vine. Burlington Avenue runs across the top; Rancocas Avenue runs down from it near the creek and continues further east below Buttonwood, Franklin runs down the middle, and Vine along the right edge. Buttonwood, Ash and Poplar cross the sheet, each with a parallel alley (Buttonwood Alley, Ash Alley, Poplar Alley) through the blocks to the east of Franklin. Union Avenue and Hickory Street are named in the lower right corner. The creek front holds the industry of the town: the A. Ridgway and Son Co. factory for infants' and children's shoes, marked not in operation, with its power house and storage building and sprinkler notes; and the Rancocas Construction Co. Inc., bridge and wharf builders, with boat building sheds, a store room, an office and a launching slip with ways. The bridgeman's house stands at the steel and wood drawbridge 400 ft to Riverside, at the top left. The blocks east of Franklin are lined with frame dwellings on narrow lots, with stores and garages along Burlington Avenue, a boat yard, and a few brick-veneered buildings. Water pipes of 4 to 12 inches and hydrants are drawn along the streets. The compass rose is at the top, the scale of feet at the bottom, and sheet numbers 4 and 6 mark the adjoining sheets.
notes: Rancocas Avenue is drawn in two straight pieces with a jog at Buttonwood; OpenStreetMap has it as two separate ways, and its junction with Burlington Avenue lies several metres from the drawn one. It was left out of the control.
A. Ridgway & Son Co. shoe factory (not in operation) and the Rancocas Construction Co. bridge and wharf building yard are on this sheet.
A note at the top left reads 'Steel & Wood Draw Bridge 400' to Riverside'.

Map, 50 ft, turned like sheet 4. Burlington Av to Poplar between Rancocas Creek and Vine: Rancocas Av, Franklin, Buttonwood, Ash and Poplar with their alleys; A. Ridgway & Son Co. shoe factory and Rancocas Construction Co. boat yard. One part. Modern Rancocas Avenue does not follow the 1927 line near Burlington Av and was left out.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6, drawn at 50 ft to an inch, covers the south-western part of Delanco between Rancocas Creek and Walnut, from Hickory down to the Pennsylvania Railroad. Union Avenue runs down the middle of the sheet. East of it the grid is square: Hickory, Laurel and Mulberry cross from Union Avenue to Walnut on the right edge, split by Walnut Alley and an unnamed alley in block 38, with Pennsylvania Avenue running diagonally along the south side towards the railroad. West of Union Avenue the streets run on the diagonal grid of the creek side: Vine Street and Poplar at the top, Franklin and Pine, and Rancocas Avenue along the creek bank. The blocks are residential, mostly frame dwellings with garages, sheds and coops. The 1st Presbyterian Church with its parsonage stands on Union Avenue in block 33, the post office on Poplar, and a carpenter shop and a wagon shed in the diagonal blocks. Delanco Station of the P.R.R. stands on Pennsylvania Avenue, with the double track of the Amboy Division running along the bottom right of the sheet. Rancocas Creek fills the lower left corner. Water pipes and hydrants are drawn along the streets. The bottom margin notes no exposure beyond the railroad, the compass rose is at the upper left and the scale of feet at the lower left.
notes: Walnut Alley is lettered in two pieces, 'Alley' north of Laurel and 'Walnut' south of it.
OpenStreetMap has two junctions of Poplar Street and Rancocas Avenue about 40 m apart; both matched drawn junctions and were kept.
The 1st Presbyterian Church, the post office and Delanco Station of the Pennsylvania Railroad (Amboy Division) are on this sheet.

Map, 50 ft. Hickory to Pennsylvania Av: Union Av, Laurel, Walnut Alley, Mulberry, Walnut on the east; Poplar, Franklin, Pine and Rancocas Av on the diagonal grid by Rancocas Creek; 1st Presbyterian Church, Delanco Station, P.R.R. Amboy Division. One part.

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7, drawn at 100 ft to an inch rather than the 50 ft of the other sheets, covers the eastern half of Delanco from the Delaware River to the Pennsylvania Railroad. North of Burlington Avenue (St. Mihiel Drive), which crosses the sheet diagonally, Delaware Avenue, 2nd Street and 3rd Street run across a grid of numbered blocks between Walnut at the left edge and Maple Avenue at the right, crossed by Holly, Hazel Avenue, Edgewood Avenue, Centre Avenue and Oakford Avenue. The river front blocks are large and lightly built; the blocks further south hold frame dwellings with garages, and the Delanco Garage stands on Burlington Avenue in block 63. South of Burlington Avenue the sheet covers Walnut and Spruce crossed by Chestnut, Hickory and Laurel, and Cooper running south-east to Cooper Road. Block 14 holds the grounds of the Fletcher Grove Camp Meeting Association, occupied in summer only, with an auditorium, sleeping quarters and rows of small cottages. Block 43 is largely open, with the Edward Bird auto body building, a ball park with grand stands, and the L. R. Weikman coal yard by the railroad. Pennsylvania Avenue runs along the railroad at the bottom, where the double track of the Amboy Division passes the freight station and a section house. Mulberry Street is named at the bottom left. Water pipes and hydrants are drawn along the streets, the compass rose and the scale of 100 ft to an inch are printed at the right.
notes: Drawn at 100 ft to an inch; the other sheets of the atlas are at 50 ft.
Centre Avenue is the modern Center Street; Holly is Holly Avenue; Spruce is Spruce Street.
Cooper Road is probably the modern Coopertown Road.
The modern lines of Burlington Avenue (about 4 m) and Cooper Street (7 to 17 m) differ from those drawn here; neither was used as control.
Fletcher Grove Camp Meeting Association grounds, the Edward Bird auto body building, the ball park and the L. R. Weikman coal yard are on this sheet.

Map, 100 ft to an inch. Eastern half of the town: Delaware Av to the P.R.R. between Walnut and Maple Av (Holly, Hazel, Edgewood, Centre, Oakford), and Chestnut, Hickory, Laurel, Spruce, Cooper south of Burlington Av; Fletcher Grove Camp Meeting grounds, ball park, coal yard. One part. Burlington Avenue (about 4 m) and Cooper Street (7 to 17 m) are displaced against their modern lines here and were left out.
